<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par68 />the 1st ''pers.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=6}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֹסִֽפְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=6}}, which is apparently (from the {{GHGterm|Metheg}} with the ''i''), intended for an {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}}: instead of it, however, read, with the Mantua edition, {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽסִפְךָ}} (with ''ĭ'', according to {{GHGpar|60|f}}). But {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאסִפוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=7}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תּֽוֹס׳}}), {{GHGheb|text=וַיֹּ֫אסֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=29}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַיּ֫וֹסֶף}}), and {{GHGheb|text=יאסף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=19}} (see above) are due to a mistake, since all three forms must be derived from the stem {{GHGheb|text=יָסַף}}. Furthermore, {{GHGheb|text=יֽׄמְר֫וּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=20}} (where certainly {{GHGheb|text=יַמְר׳}} is to be read); {{GHGheb|text=תֹּבֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=10}} (cf. {{GHGpar|75|hh}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּפֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=יוֹכְלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=42|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽמְרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתֹּ֫חֶז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽוְלִי|translate=thou gaddest about}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אָזַל}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=36}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫תֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=21}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יֶֽאֱתֶה}}), according to other readings (on the analogy of the cases mentioned in {{GHGpar|75|p}}) {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵתֵ֫א}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫תֶא}} or {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּ֫תֶא}}.

Paradigm I shows the weak forms of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, and merely indicates the other conjugations, which are regular.

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|i}}
Rem. 1. In the derived conjugations only isolated weak forms occur: {{GHGterm|Perfect Niphal}} {{GHGheb|text=נֹֽאחֲזוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=9}}; ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫אצֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} (but the statement in verse 17 is {{GHGheb|text=וְאָֽצַלְתִּי}}, therefore Qal); equally doubtful is the punctuation of {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רֶב}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽאֲרֵב}}?) ''and he laid wait'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=5}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אָזִין|translate=I listen}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=11}} (on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}); cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אוֹכִיל}} (''ô'' from ''â'') ''I give to eat'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hos|chapter=11|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֹבִ֫ידָה}} (''ô'' from ''â'') ''I will destroy'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיּוֹחֶר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=5}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (for {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּאח׳}}); the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} appears to require the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְיַחֵר}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יחר}} as a secondary form of {{GHGheb|text=אחר}}; but {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּיחַר}}={{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּאחַר}} for {{GHGheb|text=וַיֶּֽאֱחַר}} as {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} is not impossible. On {{GHGheb|text=וָאֽוֹצְרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=13}}, cf. {{GHGpar|53|n}}.—{{GHGterm|Infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=לְהָכִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=33}} (={{GHGheb|text=לְהַֽאֲכ׳}} unless it is rather ''infin. Hiph.'' from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}); {{GHGterm|Participle}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵזִין|translate=giveth ear}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=4}} (clearly by false analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, for {{GHGheb|text=מַֽאֲזִין}}); {{GHGterm|Imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵתָ֫יוּ|translate=bring}} (from {{GHGheb|text=אָתָה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=9}}. (On the same form used for the {{GHGterm|perfect}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGpar|76|d}}.)

{{GHGmargin-letter|68|k}}
2. In the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} the {{GHGheb|text=א}} is sometimes elided (like {{GHGheb|text=ה}} in {{GHGheb|text=יְהַקְטִיל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַקְטִיל}}), thus {{GHGheb|text=מַלֵּף}} (as in Aramaic and Samaritan) ''teaching'', for {{GHGheb|text=מְאַלֵּף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=35|verse=11}}; {{GHGheb|text=יַהֵל}} (if not a mere scribal error) for {{GHGheb|text=יְאַהֵל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=13|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתַּזְרֵ֫נִי|translate=thou hast girded me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=40}}, for {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַזְּרֵ֫נִי}} as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=40}}; {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאַבֶּדְּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=16}}; cf. {{GHGpar|23|c}}.<section end=par68 />

<section begin=par69 />{{GHGpar-heading|69|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}. First Class, or Verbs originally {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁב}} to dwell}}

<div style="font-size: small; text-align: center;">Brockelmann, {{GHGcite|title=Semit. Sprachwiss.}}, p. 141 f.; {{GHGcite|title=Grundriss}}, p. 596 ff.</div>

{{GHGmargin-letter|69|a}}
Verbs which at present begin with Yôdh when without preformatives are divided into two classes according to their origin and consequent inflexion: (''a'') Verbs which (as still in Arabic and Ethiopic) originally began with {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָלַד|translate=to give birth to}}, Arab. and Eth. ''wălădă''. In consequence of a phonetic change which prevails also with few exceptions in the noun, this {{GHGterm|Wāw}} in Hebrew and Aramaic always becomes a {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, at least when it is the initial consonant; but after preformatives it either reappears, or is again changed into<section end=par69 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
